Our Story

One space, two reasons to stop.

Karen Baobab Classic Gallery & Café sits on Comboni Road, next to Tangaza University — a working gallery of Kenyan art and hand-carved craft, built around a café serving Kenyan cooking. You can browse first and eat after, or the other way round.

The Gallery

Kenyan art & hand-carved craft

Wood sculpture, traditional masks, paintings, textiles and souvenirs — made by Kenyan artists and craftsmen, filling every shelf of the space.

The Café

Classic Kenyan cooking

Pilau, nyama choma, ugali and chapati, plus coffee and cold drinks — seating inside and under umbrellas outside, open daily 7am–8pm.

Gallery & Curio Shop

What you'll find on the shelves

A working collection, always changing — this is a taste of what's in the space, not the full inventory.

Hand-Carved Wood Sculpture

Life-sized Maasai figures, animal carvings and statuettes, shaped by hand from local hardwood.

Carved Wildlife Pieces

Giraffes, elephants and Big Five figures, from tabletop size to statement pieces for a room.

Traditional Masks

Carved and painted masks in a range of styles, hung wall-to-wall through the gallery.

Kenyan Fashion & Textiles

Dashikis, kikoys, kangas and beaded belts, alongside safari hats and everyday wear.

Painted Curios & Keepsakes

Hand-painted bowls, animal figurines and small carvings, easy to pack and take home.

Souvenirs & Gifts

Fridge magnets, mugs, chess sets and small Kenya-themed keepsakes for every budget.

Buying a piece? Stop by Comboni Road to see the full collection in person, or call 0711 142 595 to ask about a specific piece before you visit.
The Café

Classic Kenyan cooking

Indoor seating, an outdoor patio under umbrellas, and a counter for coffee and cold drinks.

Pilau
